question: Where does the oesophagus typically begin in the neck?
explanation: The oesophagus starts right at the lower border of the cricoid cartilage, which lines up with the sixth cervical vertebra. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h1)

question: When swallowing a sharp object, it might get stuck near the aortic arch. Which structure lies right in front of the oesophagus here?
explanation: As the oesophagus travels down the chest, the aortic arch and the left main bronchus cross right in front of it, creating natural narrow spots. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h1)

question: What kind of tissue lines a healthy adult oesophagus?
explanation: The inner lining of the oesophagus uses tough stratified squamous cells to protect against friction and physical damage from swallowed food. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h2)

question: How does the muscle layer change as you move down the length of the oesophagus?

options.A: Striated skeletal muscle transitions into smooth muscle
options.B: Circular muscle fibers disappear while longitudinal fibers remain
options.C: The muscular layer is replaced entirely by serosa
options.D: Smooth muscle transitions entirely into skeletal muscle

explanation: The top third has skeletal muscle so you can swallow voluntarily, which gradually changes into smooth muscle in the lower two-thirds. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h2)

question: Where does the lower section of the oesophagus send its venous blood?

options.B: Portal venous system via the left gastric vein
options.C: Inferior vena cava via azygous veins
options.D: Superior vena cava via brachiocephalic veins

explanation: Blood from the lower part of the oesophagus drains straight into the left gastric vein, which connects directly to the portal vein system. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why does liver cirrhosis often lead to bleeding in the lower oesophagus?

options.A: Blocked liver blood flow backs up pressure into the portosystemic anastomoses at the lower oesophagus
options.B: Low systemic blood pressure destroys the muscular walls of the middle oesophagus
options.C: Increased inferior vena cava pressure dilates the upper thoracic veins
options.D: Excess bile production erodes the stratified squamous lining of the mucosa

explanation: Cirrhosis blocks blood flow through the liver, raising pressure in the portal system and forcing blood into smaller collateral vessels near the stomach. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve controls the main parasympathetic movements of the oesophagus walls?
explanation: The vagus nerve provides the parasympathetic signals that drive wave-like muscle contractions along the entire length of the tube. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main job of the myenteric plexus found between the muscle layers of the oesophagus?

options.A: Coordinating rhythmic muscular contractions for peristalsis
options.B: Transmitting conscious pain sensations to the cerebral cortex
options.C: Secreting protective mucus onto the mucosal surface
options.D: Regulating local blood flow from the thoracic aorta

explanation: The myenteric plexus inside the muscle layer controls the timing of contractions and relaxations needed to push food downward. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h4)

question: What triggers secondary peristalsis in the oesophagus if food gets left behind after a normal swallow?

options.A: Local distension and stretching of the oesophagal wall
options.B: Stimulation of the glossopharyngeal nerve in the pharynx
options.C: Increased secretion of saliva from the parotid glands
options.D: Activation of somatic motor fibers in the tongue

explanation: When leftover food stretches the oesophagus wall, local nerve reflexes automatically start a secondary wave to clear it out. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h5)

question: A patient takes medication while lying completely flat. How does the pill still reach the stomach?

options.A: Active peristaltic waves push the tablet downward regardless of posture
options.B: The submucosal glands secrete high volumes of fluid to wash it down
options.C: Respiratory movements create a vacuum that pulls contents through
options.D: Intra-abdominal pressure forces gastric acid upward to dissolve the pill

explanation: Active, sequential muscle squeezes in the oesophagus wall push food and medicine along, even if you are lying down. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which muscle forms the main part of the upper oesophageal sphincter?
explanation: The cricopharyngeus muscle stays contracted to keep the upper sphincter closed and prevent air from entering the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which option is NOT a way the lower oesophageal sphincter prevents acid reflux?

options.A: Positive intra-abdominal pressure keeping the junction closed
options.B: Pinch-cock compression from the right crus of the diaphragm
options.C: Intrinsic smooth muscle tone of the sphincter itself
options.D: Active secretion of protective alkaline mucus by the sphincter

explanation: The lower oesophageal sphincter relies on muscle tone, diaphragm support, and natural pressure differences, not mucus production, to stop reflux. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main problem in a patient with achalasia of the oesophagus?

options.A: Hypersecretion of hydrochloric acid by the lower oesophageal glands
options.B: Inflammation caused by chronic ingestion of excessively hot liquids
options.C: Excessive resting pressure and failure of the lower oesophageal sphincter to relax
options.D: Complete destruction of the upper oesophagal sphincter by infection

explanation: Achalasia happens when nerve cells in the muscle wall die off, meaning the lower sphincter cannot relax to let food pass into the stomach. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h7)

question: A patient with long-term heartburn has an endoscopy, and a biopsy shows Barrett's oesophagus. What cellular change happened?

options.A: The muscularis propria has undergone permanent atrophy
options.B: Columnar cells have mutated into striated muscle fibers
options.C: Smooth muscle has been replaced by fibrous scar tissue
options.D: Squamous epithelium has transformed into columnar epithelium

explanation: Constant exposure to stomach acid causes the normal flat skin-like lining of the lower oesophagus to change into a more resistant columnar type. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h7)
